1.note: Jeremiah is using **the word of Yahweh was to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh gave me a message.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke a message to me, saying]

Jeremiah is using the words translated as **And the word of Yahweh was to me** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

2.q: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְ⁠קָֽרָאתָ֩ בְ⁠אָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem that I, Yahweh, say this]

Here, **the ears of Jerusalem** represents the hearing of the people who live in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the people who live in Jerusalem so that they hear it]

The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the city of Jerusalem as though she were one woman, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how you were faithful to my covenant when you were young]

Yahweh is speaking as if the early days of the nation of Israel were a person’s **youth**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the covenant faithfulness of your early days as a nation]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **love**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how you loved me in the early days of our relationship]

Yahweh is speaking as if the beginning of his covenant relationship with Israel were the time of **your betrothal**, when a man and a woman were promised to each other before their marriage. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the love you had when I first bound myself to you]

The expression **not sown** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in the land where no one had planted crops]

3.note: Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person, as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [Israel was holy to me, Yahweh]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel were **the first of his harvest**, the first portion of a crop that belonged to him alone. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the portion that belonged only to him]

Yahweh is speaking as if the nations who harmed Israel were people who **ate** what belonged to him alone. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All those who harmed it became guilty]

In the phrase **the declaration of Yahweh**, Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person by name. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [this is my declaration]

4.note: The terms **house of Jacob** and the house of **Israel** mean the same thing. **Jacob** and **Israel** are two names for the same person. Jeremiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [you people of Israel, descendants of Jacob]
The imperative **Hear** is plural here because Jeremiah is addressing all the people of Israel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here, **the word of Yahweh** represents the message that Yahweh is speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Hear what Yahweh is telling you]

Jeremiah is speaking as if the descendants of Jacob were a single **house**, that is, one household. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people descended from Jacob]

5.note: Jeremiah is using **Thus says Yahweh** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

5.q: מַה־מָּצְא֨וּ אֲבוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֥ם בִּ⁠י֙ עָ֔וֶל כִּ֥י רָחֲק֖וּ מֵ⁠עָלָ֑⁠י וַ⁠יֵּֽלְכ֛וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַ⁠הֶ֖בֶל וַ⁠יֶּהְבָּֽלוּ
5.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the Israelites and to emphasize that their fathers had no valid reason for abandoning him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Your fathers did not find anything wrong in me, and yet they went far away from me and went after worthless idols and became worthless.]

Yahweh is speaking as if the ancestors of the people of Israel were their **fathers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your forefathers]

Yahweh is speaking as if abandoning their relationship with him were moving to a distant place, since he says that the ancestors **went far away from** him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that they abandoned me]

Yahweh is speaking as if worshiping idols were following behind them, since he says that the ancestors **went after** the empty. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they worshiped worthless idols]
Here, **the empty** represents worthless idols. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [useless idols]

6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And they did not ask where Yahweh is]

The people would have been using the question form to express their need for Yahweh to help them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [How we need Yahweh, who brought us up from the land of Egypt!]

Yahweh is speaking as if the deadly danger of the wilderness were **thick darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in a land of dryness and deadly peril]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and no one lives there?’]

7.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the land that belongs to me]

Yahweh is speaking as if the sins of his people were dirt that **defiled** his land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But you came and made my land unacceptable to me by your sins]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **an abomination**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and you made my inheritance utterly disgusting to me]

8.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the men who taught his law took hold of it with their hands, calling them **the handlers of the law**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and those who taught the law]

Yahweh is speaking as if the leaders of his people were **shepherds** who cared for a flock of sheep. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and those who shepherded my people transgressed against me]

Yahweh is speaking as if worshiping idols, **things not profitable**, were following behind them, since he says that the prophets **walked after** things that were not profitable. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and worshiped things that are not profitable]

9.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result]

Yahweh is speaking as if his dispute with his people were a **case** that he would argue with them in a court of law. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will still confront you about your wrongdoing]

Yahweh is speaking as if the later descendants of his people were **the sons of your sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your later descendants]

10.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [To understand this,]

Yahweh is referring to all of the surrounding nations by naming two major components, **the coasts of Kittim** in the far west and **Kedar** in the east. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the surrounding nations in every direction and look, and to them]
The word **Kittim** is the name of a coastal region in the sea west of Israel.

11.q: הַ⁠הֵימִ֥יר גּוֹי֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְ⁠הֵ֖מָּה לֹ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים
11.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no other nation has ever exchanged its gods, even though those gods are not real. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [No nation has ever exchanged its gods, though they were not gods!]

The implication is that **their glory** is Yahweh himself, the God who gave his people their honor. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the God who is their glory]

Here, **does not profit** represents idols that give no benefit to those who worship them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [idols that give them no benefit]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking to the **heavens**, which he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about how his people have abandoned him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the heavens. Alternate translation: [Let the heavens be appalled at this]

Yahweh is speaking of the **heavens** as if they were a living thing that could **shudder** in horror. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let this be a scene of horror and utter desolation]

13.note: Yahweh is speaking as if he himself were **the spring of living waters**, a source of fresh water that never fails. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They have abandoned me, their never-failing source life-sustaining water]

Yahweh is using **living waters** as a common expression of the culture to mean “fresh water that flows from a spring.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [flowing fresh water]

**Cisterns** are pits dug in the ground and lined with plaster in order to store rainwater. If your readers would not be familiar with what cisterns are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [to dig out water storage pits for themselves, broken pits]

13.q: בֹּארֹת֙ נִשְׁבָּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא יָכִ֖לוּ הַ⁠מָּֽיִם
13.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the idols that his people worship were **broken cisterns that do not hold the water**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that is, useless idols that give them no help]

14.q: הַ⁠עֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָ⁠בַֽז
14.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that Israel is not a slave and so should not have been carried away by enemies. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Israel is not a servant! He is not a slave born in his master’s house! So he should never have been carried off as plunder!]

14.q: הַ⁠עֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָ⁠בַֽז
14.note: Even though Yahweh is addressing his people directly, he is speaking about them in the third person as **Israel** and as **he**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [Israel, are you a servant? Were you born a slave in your master’s house? So why have you become plunder]

The implication is that a **homeborn** slave was one who was born to slaves in his master’s household and so belonged to that household from birth. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a slave born in his master’s household]

Yahweh is using the question form to draw attention to how strange it is that a people who were not slaves have been carried off by their enemies. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [So it is astounding that he has been carried off as plunder!]

15.note: The pronoun **him** refers to the people of Israel, whom Yahweh described in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Young lions roared against the people of Israel]

Yahweh is speaking as if the enemy armies that attacked his people were **Young lions** roaring as they seized their prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Fierce enemy armies shouted war cries against him]

Yahweh is using **they gave their voice** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they roared loudly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they roared loudly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **a desolation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And they made his land desolate]

16.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the people who lived in these cities were **the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes]
The words **Memphis** and **Tahpanhes** are the names of cities in Egypt.

Shaving the top of a person’s head was a symbolic action by which conquerors showed that they had defeated and humiliated the one whose head they shaved. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [have shaved the crown of your head, showing that they have conquered and humiliated you]

17.q: הֲ⁠לוֹא־זֹ֖את תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֑⁠ךְ עָזְבֵ⁠ךְ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִ⁠ךְ בְּ⁠עֵ֖ת מוֹלִיכֵ֥⁠ךְ בַּ⁠דָּֽרֶךְ
17.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that his people brought this disaster on themselves. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have certainly brought this on yourself when you abandoned Yahweh your God at the time he was leading you in the way!]

17.q: הֲ⁠לוֹא זֹ֖את תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּ֑⁠ךְ עָזְבֵ⁠ךְ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִ⁠ךְ בְּ⁠עֵ֖ת מוֹלִיכֵ֥⁠ךְ בַּ⁠דָּֽרֶךְ
17.note: The word that the ULT translates as **when** indicates that Yahweh **led you in the way** at the same time as when his people **abandoned** him. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [Have you not brought this to yourself when you abandoned Yahweh your God at the very time that he was leading you in the way]

Even though Yahweh is the one who is speaking, he is speaking about himself in the third person as **Yahweh your God**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [when you abandoned me, Yahweh your God, when I led you in the way]

Yahweh is speaking as if the manner of life that he wanted his people to follow were **the way**, a road along which he led them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when he was directing you how to live]

18.q: וְ⁠עַתָּ֗ה מַה־לָּ⁠ךְ֙ לְ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם & וּ⁠מַה־לָּ⁠ךְ֙ לְ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר
18.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And now, why do you set out on the road to Egypt … And why do you set out on the road to Assyria]

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for seeking help from Egypt. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And now, it does you no good to travel the road to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile! And it does you no good to travel the road to Assyria to drink the waters of the River!]

Yahweh is speaking as if making an alliance with Egypt were traveling there **to drink the waters of the Nile**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to rely on Egypt for support]

The word **River** represents the country of Assyria, through which the Euphrates River flows. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to drink the waters of that country]

19.note: Yahweh is speaking of the **evil** of his people as if it were a living thing that could **rebuke** them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will rebuke you because of your evil]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **apostasy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the fact that you turned away from me will punish you]

The terms **know** and **see** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [So understand clearly]

The terms **evil** and **bitter** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [it is utterly disastrous]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **the fear of me**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and you do not fear me]
The word **Yahweh** is the name of God, which he revealed to his people in the Old Testament.

20.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the slavery from which he freed his people were a **yoke** and **fetters** that he broke. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For from long ago I set you free from slavery]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [But you said that you would not serve.]

The implication is that to **serve** here means to worship and obey Yahweh. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [‘I will not worship and obey you]

20.q: כִּ֣י עַֽל כָּל גִּבְעָ֞ה גְּבֹהָ֗ה וְ⁠תַ֨חַת֙ כָּל עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֔ן
20.note: The implication is that **on every high hill** and **beneath every leafy tree** were the places where the people set up shrines and worshiped idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For at the shrines on every high hill and beneath every leafy tree]
Yahweh is using the word **yourself** to emphasize that his people themselves are the ones who have acted this way. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate this emphasis.

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were a woman who would **lie down** with other men as a **prostitute**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you yourself worship other gods, acting unfaithfully to me]

21.note: Yahweh is using the word **myself** to emphasize that he was the one who planted his people. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate this emphasis.

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were **a choice vine** that he had planted. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I myself established you to be like a choice vine]

Yahweh is using the question form to express his dismay at how his people have changed toward him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [But you have surely changed towards me into degenerates of the strange vine!]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **degenerates** that are characterized by belonging to **the strange vine**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [into degenerates that belong to the strange vine]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people had become **degenerates of the strange vine**, the worthless shoots of a wild vine rather than the good vine that he planted. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [corrupt and worthless people who are of no use to me]

22.q: כִּ֤י אִם תְּכַבְּסִי֙ בַּ⁠נֶּ֔תֶר וְ⁠תַרְבִּי לָ֖⁠ךְ בֹּרִ֑ית
22.note: Yahweh is speaking as if his people could remove their guilt by washing themselves **with natron** or with **lye**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For even if you try your hardest to make yourself innocent, using every means at your disposal]

Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that his people might try to clean themselves with natron and lye. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [For even if you should clean yourself with natron]

The words **natron** and **lye** refer to kinds of cleaning agents. Natron is a mineral salt, and lye is made from the ashes of burned plants. If your readers would not be familiar with what these are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with a strong detergent or lots of cleansing powder]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the wrong things you have done remain a stain before my face]

Yahweh is speaking as if the guilt of his people were **a stain** that could not be washed out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your guilt remains inescapable before my face]
Here, **my face** represents my sight. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my sight]

23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [How can you say that you are not defiled and have not walked after the Baals?]

23.q: אֵ֣יךְ תֹּאמְרִ֞י לֹ֣א נִטְמֵ֗אתִי אַחֲרֵ֤י הַ⁠בְּעָלִים֙ לֹ֣א הָלַ֔כְתִּי
23.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for denying that they have worshiped idols. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not say, ‘I am not defiled; I have not worshiped the Baals’!]

The expression **defiled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I have not made myself unclean]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **defiled**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [I am pure]

The people are speaking as if worshiping idols were following behind them, since they claim that they have not **walked after the Baals**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have not given myself to the Baals’]

Yahweh is speaking as if the habitual conduct of his people were a **path** that they had worn into the ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Look at how you have behaved in the valleys]

The implication is that **the valleys** were the places where the people of Judah worshiped their idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the valleys where you worshiped idols]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were **a swift female camel** running back and forth in search of a mate. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are like a swift female camel]

Yahweh is using **entangling her ways** as a common expression of the culture to mean “running back and forth so that her tracks cross one another.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [crisscrossing her tracks as she runs back and forth in search of a mate]

24.note: Yahweh is speaking as if his people were **a wild donkey** that no one is able to control. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You behave like an untamable wild donkey, at home in the wilderness]

The expression **taught ones** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [one that the wilderness has taught]

Yahweh is using **sniffing at the air** as a common expression of the culture to mean “eagerly searching for a mate.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in her lust, eagerly searching for a mate]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to hold such an animal back. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [In her heat, no one at all can turn her away!]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **tire**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [All of the ones seeking her will remain fresh]

The pronoun **her** refers to the wild donkey that Yahweh has just described as an image of his people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [When that wild donkey is in heat]

25.note: Here, **your foot** and **your throat** represent the wearying effort of running after other gods. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Stop wearing yourself out running after other gods until you are barefoot and parched]

The people are using **hopeless** as a common expression of the culture to mean “it is useless to try to stop us.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [It is no use trying to stop me]

The people are speaking as if the foreign gods that they worship were **strangers** whom they loved. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for I love the gods of other nations]

26.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a thief** is disgraced when he is caught, so **the house of Israel** is disgraced now that its guilt has been exposed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as a thief is disgraced when he is caught stealing, now that their guilt has been exposed]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **thief**. He means thieves in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any thief]

The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when someone catches him]

The expression **has been put to shame** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so the house of Israel has become ashamed]

In this verse, the word **house** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of Israel as a group, and so Yahweh continues with the plural **they**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “house.” Alternate translation: [the houses of Israel, their kings, their princes]

27.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [the ones who say to the tree that it is their father … and to the stone that it gave birth to them … But in the time of their trouble they tell me to arise and save them]

Here, **the tree** represents an idol made of wood. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the idol made of wood, ‘You are my father]

Here, **the stone** represents an idol carved from stone. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and to the stone idol, ‘You gave birth to me]

27.q: כִּֽי פָנ֥וּ אֵלַ֛⁠י עֹ֖רֶף וְ⁠לֹ֣א פָנִ֑ים
27.note: Yahweh is using the expression about turning the **back to me** and not the **faces** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they have rejected me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For they have rejected me and refused to acknowledge me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **trouble**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [But when they are suffering, they say]

The people are using **Arise** as a common expression of the culture to mean “take action.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Take action and rescue us]

28.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the idols his people have made are unable to help them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [But your gods that you made for yourself are nowhere to be found!]

Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that the gods his people made might be able to save them. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If they are able to save you, let them arise]

Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will certainly not arise, because they cannot save you]

28.q: כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔י⁠ךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖י⁠ךָ יְהוּדָֽה
28.note: Yahweh says **for the number of your cities** as an extreme statement for emphasis, meaning that the people of Judah have as many gods as they have cities. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [for you have gods everywhere you look, Judah, as if there were one in every city]

28.q: כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔י⁠ךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖י⁠ךָ יְהוּדָֽה
28.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about how many gods the people of Judah have before the information about how many cities they have. Alternate translation: [for your gods, they are so many, as many as the number of your cities]

29.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for complaining against him when they have no grounds for doing so. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have no right to complain to me!]
The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing all the people of Judah, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

30.note: Yahweh is using **For futility** as a common expression of the culture to mean “without any result.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Without any result, I have struck your sons]

The implication is that when Yahweh **struck** the people, he was punishing them in order to correct them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I have punished your sons in order to correct them]

Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [your children]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **discipline**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [They kept rejecting discipline]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **discipline**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [They would not accept being corrected]

Yahweh is speaking of **Your sword** as if it were a living thing that could **devour** people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have killed your prophets with your sword]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a destructive lion** kills without mercy, so the people of Judah have killed the prophets whom Yahweh sent to them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [killing them without mercy, as a lion kills its prey]

31.note: Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of indignation at the way his people have behaved. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [What a generation you are]
The imperative **See** is plural here because, by implication, Yahweh is addressing all the people of Israel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

31.q: הֲ⁠מִדְבָּ֤ר הָיִ֨יתִי֙ לְ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֛ם אֶ֥רֶץ מַאְפֵּ֖לְיָ֑ה
31.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that he has always provided well for his people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I have certainly not been a wilderness to Israel, nor a land of thick darkness!]

Yahweh is speaking as if failing to provide for his people would make him **a wilderness to Israel**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Have I been a place without provision to Israel]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Why do my people say that they will roam free, that they will not come to me anymore]

31.q: מַדּ֜וּעַ אָמְר֤וּ עַמִּ⁠י֙ רַ֔דְנוּ לֽוֹא־נָב֥וֹא ע֖וֹד אֵלֶֽי⁠ךָ
31.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for claiming that they are free from him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [How dare my people say, ‘We shall roam free, we shall not go to you anymore’!]

The people are using **We shall roam free** as a common expression of the culture to mean “we will do whatever we please.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [We will do whatever we please]

The pronoun **you** refers to Yahweh, not to the people whom Jeremiah is addressing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [we shall not go to you, Yahweh, anymore’?]

32.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that a young woman would never forget to wear her jewelry. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [A virgin would never forget her jewelry, nor a bride her sashes!]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [or will a bride forget her sashes]

Yahweh is using **days without number** as a common expression of the culture to mean “for a very long time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for a very long time]

33.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [How shamefully you pursue your lovers]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were a woman who would **seek love** from many men. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [eagerly you go after other gods]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **love**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to seek someone to love]

Yahweh says that his people have taught **the wicked women** their own ways as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [so well that you even teach evildoers how to do evil]

Yahweh is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [to the women who are wicked]

The phrase **you taught** follows a reading in which the people of Judah are the ones who teach. The standard written text in the original language reads “I taught” instead, and most translations follow that reading. You may want to follow the reading of the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [I have instructed]

34.note: The expression **has been found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Also people have found on your skirts]

Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the guilt of his people and their refusal to admit that guilt. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yet]

The implication is that the blood on the clothing of the people is evidence that they have murdered innocent people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Also, as proof that you have killed them, on your skirts people have found]

Here, **the blood of the lives** represents evidence of violent killing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [evidence of the violent killing of the poor innocent ones]

The expression **were not discovered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one caught them committing burglary]

The implication is that the law permitted a person to kill a thief who was caught breaking in, but these poor people were not thieves, so there was no excuse for killing them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They were not caught breaking in, so you had no right to kill them]

35.note: The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [the reason is]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [you also say that you are innocent and that surely his nose has turned away from you]

The people are using **his nose has turned away from me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he is no longer angry with me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [surely he is no longer angry with me]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to judge you]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **sinned**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [I have done what is right]

36.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke his people for changing their allegiance so casually. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You act far too casually as you repeatedly change your ways!]

Yahweh is using **treat very lightly** as a common expression of the culture to mean “change your loyalties without serious thought.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are you so casually willing]

Yahweh is using **be shamed from Egypt** as a common expression of the culture to mean “be disappointed by the help that Egypt gives you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You will also be disappointed by the help Egypt gives you]

37.note: The implication is that when Yahweh says that the people will **go out**, he means that their enemies will take them away into exile. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You will also be taken away into exile from this place]

Putting **your hands on your head** was a symbolic action by which people in this culture showed that they were grieving and ashamed. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and you will put your hands on your head to show your grief and shame]

Even though Yahweh is the one who is speaking, he is speaking about himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [for I, Yahweh, have rejected the ones you trusted]

The pronoun **them** refers to Egypt and Assyria, the nations that the people of Judah trusted for help. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and you will not be successful by Egypt and Assyria]
